author: Latham, 1801
status: 나그네새 수만 마리 · 여름철새 수천 마리
habitat: 해안·섬의 암벽, 고산 암석 굴, 오래된 높은 건물
summary: 우리나라에서 드물지 않게 번식하는 여름철새로, 해안과 섬의 암벽, 높은 산의 바위굴, 오래된 높은 건물 등에 산다. 높은 하늘을 날며 먹이를 찾고, 혼자일 때도 있지만 대개 큰 무리를 이루며 짝짓기도 공중에서 한다. 6~7월에 알을 2~3개 낳는다. 파리, 딱정벌레, 벌, 매미 무리처럼 날아다니는 곤충을 주로 먹으며, 날개 길이는 17~18cm쯤이다.

art.subject: Pacific Swift (Apus pacificus), adult in flight, as seen over Korean coasts and islands from May to August: whole body sooty blackish-brown with a faint bluish gloss on the upperwing and tail; a narrow but clear white band across the rump; whitish chin and throat patch with fine dark shaft streaks, merging into dull dark-brown lores, cheeks and neck sides; underparts blackish-brown with fine pale scaling from whitish feather fringes. Bill tiny, black, with a very wide gape. Dark brown eye. Tiny black feet, usually tucked in flight.
art.pose: flying high in a loose flock, hawking insects
art.scene: Korean coastal island with sheer sea cliffs under a summer sky; no people, buildings or text
views: adult in flight seen from below, head, body and tail in one line: scythe-shaped dark wings, blackish-brown underparts with fine pale scaling, white throat patch, deeply forked tail
adult in flight seen from above, head, body and tail in one line: dark upperwing and back, narrow white band across the rump, forked brownish-black tail with a faint blue gloss
adult, head detail in profile: tiny black bill with a very wide gape, whitish chin and throat with brown shaft streaks, dull dark brown cheeks, dark eye
art.build: Medium-large swift, 20cm, longer than a Barn Swallow and with much longer, narrower scythe-shaped wings; slim cigar-shaped body, short neck, small head. Bill very short but gape extremely wide. Legs very short with four strong, sharply curved claws, used only for clinging to cliffs and walls. When clinging the wingtips extend far beyond the tail tip. Tail fairly long and deeply forked, the fork often closed to a point in fast flight. Flies fast and high with stiff, flickering wingbeats and long glides.
avoid: Do not paint swallow-like pale underparts, a red throat or thin tail streamers; swifts are dark all over.
Do not omit the narrow white rump band; it is the key feature from above.
Do not paint a square tail with a broad white rump (House Swift, Apus nipalensis).
Do not perch it on a branch or wire; swifts only cling to vertical rock or walls.
